source.title: Linking RDoC and HiTOP: A new interface for advancing psychiatric nosology and neuroscience

confidence_rationale: Directly addresses the part of Q-064 the HiTOP meta-analysis does not: it provides an explicit mapping between RDoC's neuroscience-rooted biobehavioral SYSTEMS (the vulnerability/mechanism side) and HiTOP's symptom-covariation DIMENSIONS (the expression side), which is the literature analogue of Q-064's required separation of axis-PREDISPOSITION (which mechanisms are fragile) from axis-EXPRESSION (which symptom dimension is realized). Supports the two-layer vector design. Held at 0.73 because it is a conceptual review proposing an interface, not an empirical validation that the two layers are dissociable.
failure_signatures: The RDoC<->HiTOP mapping is many-to-many and incomplete: a single biobehavioral system maps to several symptom dimensions and vice versa, so a clean one-mechanism-one-axis vulnerability vector is not guaranteed -- the pleiotropy case is the rule, not the exception, which stresses the registry design but is exactly what Q-064 anticipates.

Neither framework yet supplies validated biobehavioral grounding for every dimension, so REE cannot assume an ARC-086 axis is mechanistically real just because a corresponding symptom dimension exists (echoes the non-degeneracy precondition).

mapping.source_claim_statement: RDoC (neuroscience-rooted transdiagnostic biobehavioral systems) and HiTOP (dimensional classification derived from symptom covariation) have complementary strengths; the authors construct a comprehensive mapping between RDoC constructs/subconstructs and HiTOP spectra/subfactors, arguing RDoC can supply the biobehavioral underpinnings of HiTOP's clinical dimensions while HiTOP supplies psychometrically robust targets for RDoC research, envisaging a unified dimensional, biobehaviorally-grounded nosology.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-064 requires keeping axis-PREDISPOSITION (which vulnerability mechanisms are fragile) separable from axis-EXPRESSION (which failure mode is currently expressed, gated by developmental/plasticity machinery). The RDoC (mechanistic systems) vs HiTOP (expressed symptom dimensions) two-layer interface is the field's working instance of exactly that separation: the same biobehavioral vulnerability profile can, under different conditions, surface as different positions on the symptom spectra.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a proposed interface, not a demonstration that predisposition and expression are empirically dissociable; the mapping between RDoC systems and HiTOP dimensions is many-to-many and acknowledged to be incomplete, so it supports the FORM of Q-064's two-layer vector but does not validate that REE's ARC-086 axes will factor predisposition from expression without collapse.
mapping.source_context: Narrative review / conceptual synthesis mapping two human dimensional psychiatric frameworks (research and clinical) onto each other.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative, widely-cited synthesis from HiTOP/RDoC leaders (source_quality good for a review). Mapping_fidelity good for the predisposition/expression-factoring sub-question specifically. Transfer risk moderate: the mechanistic-vs-symptom two-layer logic transfers cleanly to REE's vulnerability-vs-expression design, but the human frameworks' incompleteness means it licenses the design, not its success.
